questions.title: The party arrival
questions.setup: You walk into a friend's party. Twenty people are already there and the room is loud.

answers.text: Scan for someone you already know, post up near them, stay there.
Find the friend who invited you, get the lay of the land, ease in.
Make a slow lap, see who looks interesting, pick a conversation.
Head straight for the snack table.

questions.title: The wide-open Saturday
questions.setup: Nothing on the calendar. By 10 a.m., where are you?

answers.text: Still in bed with a book, coffee on the nightstand.
Already out walking, running, or doing something with your body.
At your favorite spot getting breakfast and people-watching.
Deep into a project that's been on your mind all week.

questions.title: The unexpected compliment
questions.setup: A stranger pays you a real compliment in line at the store.

answers.text: You laugh, thank them warmly, think about it the rest of the day.
You say thanks, nod, move on. Nice, but you don't need it to land.
You compliment them right back. You might be friends by checkout.
You feel a little exposed and your thank-you comes out quieter than you meant.

questions.title: The phone call
questions.setup: Your phone rings. A friend. No warning, no text first.

answers.text: You pick up immediately. You love a long call.
You answer. You'd rather they'd texted, but they wouldn't call without a reason.
You let it ring. You'll get back to them in a minute.
You answer and put them on speaker while you keep doing what you were doing.

questions.title: The disagreement
questions.setup: A friend says something at dinner that you disagree with, fairly strongly.

answers.text: You push back directly, in the moment. Honesty matters between friends.
You let it pass but bring it up later when the table isn't watching.
You ask them a question that lets them rethink it themselves.
You note it and let it go. Not worth a fight tonight.

questions.title: The bedtime setup
questions.setup: What does your ideal sleep environment look like?

answers.text: Heavy blanket, cool room, blackout curtains, full dark.
Window cracked, soft sheets, the sound of rain or a fan.
A pile of pillows, your favorite person nearby, lamps on low.
Honestly, you'll fall asleep anywhere. Couch, floor, mid-sentence.

questions.title: The unexpected free hour
questions.setup: A plan you had today falls through and you've got an unexpected free hour.

answers.text: Go for a walk. Fresh air first, decide what's next after.
Sit with a snack or drink and look out a window for a while.
Squeeze in something you've been meaning to do.
Reach out to a friend or someone in your family.

questions.title: The where-to-eat pick
questions.setup: You're with a group trying to figure out where to eat. Everyone looks at you.

answers.text: The reliable favorite. No surprises tonight.
Somewhere new. Try something different.
Ask everyone what they're craving first, then decide.
Throw out two options and let the group break the tie.

questions.title: The hard day
questions.setup: It's been a rough one. You're home. What helps?

answers.text: A walk outside. Sometimes you need to physically leave the day behind.
The right person on the phone for an hour.
Comfort food, your softest clothes, a show you've already seen.
Quiet. No talking. Maybe a long bath. Definitely no plans.

questions.title: The public praise
questions.setup: A boss or teacher singles you out for praise in front of others.

answers.text: You feel warm and you let it show. You earned it.
You deflect a little, mention the team, change the subject.
You smile, say thank you, quietly enjoy it without making a thing of it.
You're uncomfortable and you crack a joke to break the tension.

questions.title: The new person
questions.setup: You're somewhere you don't really know anyone. A friendly person introduces themselves.

answers.text: You love it. Meeting a new person is the best part of your day.
You chat warmly back. You're glad they came over.
You hold up your end of the conversation, but you're ready for it to end.
You're polite but quiet. You'd rather watch the room than talk to it.

questions.title: The thing you make
questions.setup: When you've got time to make something. What feels best?

answers.text: Doing it alone, taking your time, working until it feels right.
Doing it with someone you love. Making is half the point; company is the other half.
Trying something brand new you've never done before.
Coming back to something you're already good at and getting even better.
Honestly, you'd rather watch someone else make something. Not your scene.

questions.title: The dog on the walk
questions.setup: A dog you don't know runs up to you, tail going.

answers.text: You're already crouching. New friend acquired.
You smile and let it sniff your hand. Friendly but reserved.
You step back a little. Unannounced energy is a lot.

questions.title: The surprise
questions.setup: A friend keeps a surprise from you for a week and finally tells you. It's a good one.

answers.text: You're delighted. The week of secrecy was part of the gift.
You're delighted but a little bothered they didn't tell you sooner.
You laugh and tell them next time, spoil it. Surprises stress you out.
You're touched. You'd never have done that for someone, but you love that they did it for you.

questions.title: The way you learn
questions.setup: You're trying to learn something new. What works best?

answers.text: Watching someone else do it first, then trying.
Reading about it carefully, then trying.
Diving in, making a mess, figuring it out by failing a bunch.
Having a friend or teacher walk you through it step by step.

questions.title: The sound
questions.setup: You can have one of these playing while you do your favorite thing.

answers.text: Music that matches the mood you're already in.
A book or podcast someone is reading to you.
Silence. Truly nothing.
The sounds of outside. Wind, birds, rain, faraway voices.

questions.title: The morning
questions.setup: First thing in the morning, before anyone has asked anything of you.

answers.text: You're already going. The day is light and you want to be in it.
You take your time. Breakfast slow, no rush.
You'd sleep in if anyone let you. Mornings are not your strongest hour.
You like a quiet stretch alone before the day really begins.

questions.title: The afternoon outside
questions.setup: You have a free afternoon and the weather is good. What pulls you?

answers.text: A long walk somewhere you haven't been before.
A blanket and a book under a tree.
Building, planting, or fixing something with your hands.
Watching for animals, listening to the sounds around you, paying attention.

questions.title: The hard problem
questions.setup: Something tricky has come up. A puzzle, a problem, a thing that needs figuring out.

answers.text: You go at it directly. Pick at it until it gives.
You step away. The answer usually comes when you're not looking.
You ask someone you trust to help you think it through.
You make a list. Break it down. One piece at a time.

questions.title: The kind word
questions.setup: A friend is having a really hard day. You want to help.

answers.text: You show up. Bring food. Sit with them. Don't make them talk.
You let them talk as long as they need. Listen close.
You try to make them laugh. Sometimes that's the medicine.
You give them space and check in tomorrow. Some people need quiet.

questions.title: The favorite season
questions.setup: Which one is genuinely yours?

answers.text: Summer. Light and warmth and the long evenings.
Fall. The leaves and the crisp air and the way everything turns.
Winter. Snow, quiet, candles, deep cold.
Spring. New green, new everything, the world coming back.

questions.title: The best kind of friend
questions.setup: The friendship that feels best to you is the one where…

answers.text: You can be quiet together for an hour and it doesn't feel weird.
You laugh a lot. Even when nothing's particularly funny.
You go on adventures together. Plans, trips, surprises.
You talk about the real stuff. The big questions, the hard ones.

questions.title: The waiting gap
questions.setup: You're waiting for something to start. A 15-minute gap with nothing to do.

answers.text: Phone out, immediately. Catching up on something.
People-watching. Plenty to notice if you look.
Quiet thinking. You're glad for the pause.
Up and moving. A walk anywhere not still.

questions.title: The food moment
questions.setup: The meal you'd choose if you could have any meal in the world tonight.

answers.text: Comfort food. The exact thing you grew up with, made the right way.
Something brand new. A cuisine you've never tried.
A long meal with a lot of small dishes and a lot of people you love.
Something simple and very, very good. One thing, done perfectly.

questions.title: The thing you'd hate to lose
questions.setup: If you could keep only some of these, which would feel the worst to give up?

answers.text: Long talks with the people you love.
Quiet time alone.
Music.
Travel, new places, leaving the familiar.
Anything sweet. Desserts, baked things, candy.

questions.title: The song from before
questions.setup: You hear a song you used to love come on out of nowhere.

answers.text: You sing along, even if other people are around.
You stop what you're doing and just listen.
You feel a wave of memory before you can name it.
You enjoy it for a moment, then put on something else.

questions.title: The way you dress
questions.setup: What you put on in the morning, in general, is…

answers.text: Whatever you've been comfortable in for years. You know what works.
Whatever you're in the mood for that day. It changes a lot.
The same kinds of things as the people around you. You don't want to stand out.
Something you picked specifically because no one else would have picked it.
